items.label: LLM01:2025
items.title: Prompt Injection
items.rationale: Pattern rules catch known direct and indirect injection phrasing, chat-template special tokens, jailbreak personas and instruction-hijack text inside skill files. They are regular expressions over tool inputs and plugin content: paraphrased, translated or novel injections are not reliably detected, and model-side input is not inspected by these rules.

items.label: LLM02:2025
items.title: Sensitive Information Disclosure
items.rationale: For an agent's tool calls the rules cover the main disclosure paths: reading credential, key, cloud, keychain and browser stores, known API-key formats in commands or content, and exfiltration over HTTP, DNS, archives and cloud or code repositories. Personal data inside model responses is out of scope for these rules and is handled by the separate DLP/privacy engine.

items.label: LLM03:2025
items.title: Supply Chain
items.rationale: Rules flag install-script piping, unpinned or unsigned package installs, miner packages, insecure dependency sources and malicious skill/plugin content. For models, downloads from Hugging Face organisations or hosts outside the trusted model sources, weight downloads over plain HTTP, trust_remote_code and unsafe model deserialization are held or denied. Model files are not verified by hash or signature, dataset provenance is not checked, and package reputation needs the separately deployed package-check endpoint (inert when none is configured).

items.label: LLM04:2025
items.title: Data and Model Poisoning
items.rationale: AIDR sits at the agent's tool-call boundary and never sees training or fine-tuning data, so poisoned training data and backdoored weights are not detected. Two steps are covered. The loading step through which a tampered model file runs code: torch.load without weights_only, pickle/joblib/dill on downloads, Keras safe_mode=False and numpy allow_pickle=True in code the agent writes or runs; a poisoned model in a data-only format (for example .safetensors) passes. And what an agent writes into memory and vector/RAG stores through MCP tools, which is scanned for hidden or injected instructions and standing orders before it is stored; records without those signals, and stores written outside the agent, are not detected. Runtime memory and context poisoning of an agent is tracked under ASI06.

items.label: LLM05:2025
items.title: Improper Output Handling
items.rationale: Model-generated commands and code are validated before they execute: pipe-to-shell, reverse shells, eval of decoded payloads, LOLBin and script-host execution and obfuscated command lines are denied or held for approval at the tool boundary. Code the agent writes is also checked by the secure-code guardrails (eval or shell commands built from input, SQL built by string formatting, TLS verification off, permissive CORS, exposed debuggers, CSRF off, weak crypto); those are language-gated patterns over added lines and warn by default rather than block. Output rendered in a UI (XSS, markdown links) is not covered by these rules.

items.label: LLM06:2025
items.title: Excessive Agency
items.rationale: The rule set is primarily an excessive-agency control: destructive deletion, persistence, privilege changes, security-control tampering, credential access and discovery performed through the agent's tools are denied or require out-of-band human approval.

items.label: LLM07:2025
items.title: System Prompt Leakage
items.rationale: Three rules flag system-prompt extraction requests (direct, repetition and translation tricks) in tool inputs. Leakage through model output and indirect extraction phrasing outside those patterns are not detected.

items.label: LLM08:2025
items.title: Vector and Embedding Weaknesses
items.rationale: AIDR does not operate a retrieval pipeline, vector store or embedding service, so there is nothing for a tool-call rule to inspect for this risk.

items.label: LLM09:2025
items.title: Misinformation
items.rationale: Detection rules judge what an agent does, not whether model output is true. Hallucinated-package risk is partly addressed by the separate package-reputation check, not by these rules.

items.label: LLM10:2025
items.title: Unbounded Consumption
items.rationale: Cryptominer binaries, pools, wallets and miner flags launched through an agent are blocked (compute hijacking). Token, request-rate and cost exhaustion of the model API itself are outside what these rules observe.

items.label: ASI01:2026
items.title: Agent Goal Hijack
items.rationale: Injection, triggered-instruction and hidden-instruction patterns in tool inputs and skill files are detected. Goal hijack that uses ordinary wording, or that only shows up as a changed plan, is not visible to pattern rules; the resulting harmful tool calls are still caught by the ASI02/ASI05 rules.

items.label: ASI02:2026
items.title: Tool Misuse and Exploitation
items.rationale: This is the enforcement point of the product: every rule evaluates a tool call (shell command, file path, URL or tool input) before it runs, and dangerous uses of legitimate tools are denied or held for out-of-band approval.

items.label: ASI03:2026
items.title: Identity and Privilege Abuse
items.rationale: Credential dumping, credential-store and key access, alternate-credential execution, sudo/UAC abuse, account creation and group changes, and access to AIDR's own approval key are detected. Delegated agent identity (tokens issued to the agent) is verified by the delegated-credential feature, not by these rules.

items.label: ASI04:2026
items.title: Agentic Supply Chain Vulnerabilities
items.rationale: Skill and plugin packages are scanned for injected instructions, remote payloads, embedded code, credential exfiltration and insecure dependencies, and risky install commands are flagged. Models from untrusted Hugging Face organisations or hosts, plain-HTTP weight downloads, trust_remote_code and unsafe model loading are held or denied. MCP server identity and signed manifests are enforced by the MCP gateway rather than these rules; model integrity (hash or signature) and dataset provenance are not covered.

items.label: ASI05:2026
items.title: Unexpected Code Execution (RCE)
items.rationale: Download-and-execute chains, pipe-to-shell, reverse shells, encoded or obfuscated execution, script hosts and LOLBins on Linux, macOS and Windows are denied before the command runs. Loading model files through code-executing deserializers and trust_remote_code are held or denied, and eval, shell commands built from input and network-exposed debuggers in code the agent writes are flagged by the (advisory) secure-code guardrails.

items.label: ASI06:2026
items.title: Memory & Context Poisoning
items.rationale: Content that asks the agent to persist instructions in memory, and skill files that write into agent memory or instruction files, are flagged. Every agent write to an instruction, memory, configuration or MCP file needs out-of-band approval, and the written text, memory-store writes and MCP tool descriptions are scanned for hidden Unicode and injected directives. Poisoning through ordinary-looking stored content or retrieval data is not detected.

items.label: ASI07:2026
items.title: Insecure Inter-Agent Communication
items.rationale: No rule inspects agent-to-agent messages or protocols (A2A, shared task queues). MCP traffic is inspected by the MCP gateway, which is a separate component.

items.label: ASI08:2026
items.title: Cascading Failures
items.rationale: Rules act on single tool calls on one host; they do not model failure propagation across agents or workflows. Blocking a harmful call limits blast radius but is not claimed as coverage of this risk.

items.label: ASI09:2026
items.title: Human-Agent Trust Exploitation
items.rationale: Rules flag skills that tell the agent to hide actions from the user and agent attempts to forge or self-issue the human approval AIDR requires. Persuasive or misleading agent output shown to a human is not analysed.

items.label: ASI10:2026
items.title: Rogue Agents
items.rationale: Behaviour typical of a compromised or rogue agent is detected: tampering with or disabling AIDR itself, reading or changing AIDR's canary credentials, disabling OS security controls, clearing logs and hiding artifacts. Slow behavioural drift within allowed actions is not something a per-call rule can see (the behavioural analyzer is a separate, optional detector).

items.label: AML.T0010.003
items.title: Model
items.rationale: The routes by which a compromised model reaches the agent's host are flagged: downloads from Hugging Face organisations or hosts outside the trusted model sources, weight downloads over plain HTTP, remote model code and code-executing model formats. A compromised model from a trusted publisher, or tampered weights in a data-only format, are not detected; files are not verified by hash or signature.

items.label: AML.T0010.005
items.title: AI Agent Tool
items.rationale: Skill and plugin packages are scanned before use against the T01-T09 skill risk taxonomy. Compromise of a remotely hosted tool that changes after the scan is not visible.

items.label: AML.T0011
items.title: User Execution
items.rationale: Enabling trust_remote_code (in code or on a serving command line), which runs Python shipped in a model repository, is held for approval and denied for publishers outside the trusted model sources.

items.label: AML.T0011.000
items.title: Unsafe AI Artifacts
items.rationale: Loading unsafe AI artifacts is held or denied: torch.load without weights_only, pickle/joblib/dill on downloaded files or network responses, Keras safe_mode=False, numpy allow_pickle=True and unsafe YAML loaders. The Python patterns apply to code the agent writes or runs; a loader reached through a library wrapper the patterns do not name is missed.

items.label: AML.T0011.001
items.title: Malicious Package
items.rationale: Installs of known miner packages and unsigned remote installer packages are flagged.

items.label: AML.T0012
items.title: Valid Accounts
items.rationale: Running commands under alternate user credentials (runas) is held for approval.

items.label: AML.T0025
items.title: Exfiltration via Cyber Means
items.rationale: Sensitive-file upload, DNS-label exfiltration, alternative protocols, automated exfiltration tooling and transfers to code repositories or cloud storage are detected.

items.label: AML.T0048.000
items.title: Financial Harm
items.rationale: Cryptomining through an agent (a direct financial harm to the victim) is blocked; other financial harms are out of scope.

items.label: AML.T0050
items.title: Command and Scripting Interpreter
items.rationale: Shell, PowerShell, AppleScript/JXA, Python and script-host execution patterns used for remote payloads, obfuscation and proxy execution are detected across all three OSes.

items.label: AML.T0051
items.title: LLM Prompt Injection
items.rationale: Known injection and jailbreak phrasing only; see OWASP LLM01.

items.label: AML.T0051.001
items.title: Indirect
items.rationale: Indirect-injection phrasing in tool content and instruction-hijack text in skills is detected; unseen wording is not.

items.label: AML.T0053
items.title: AI Agent Tool Invocation
items.rationale: Every tool call the agent makes is evaluated against the rules before it executes; a hijacked agent's tool invocations are the input AIDR inspects.

items.label: AML.T0054
items.title: LLM Jailbreak
items.rationale: Known jailbreak personas and tokens (DAN, developer mode) are detected.

items.label: AML.T0055
items.title: Unsecured Credentials
items.rationale: Reads, copies and archives of credential files, SSH and cloud keys, keychains, browser stores, registry credentials, cloud metadata credentials and plaintext secrets are detected.

items.label: AML.T0056
items.title: Extract LLM System Prompt
items.rationale: Three system-prompt extraction patterns; see OWASP LLM07.

items.label: AML.T0068
items.title: LLM Prompt Obfuscation
items.rationale: Hidden or encoded instructions, zero-width and Unicode tag characters, bidi controls and hidden HTML comments are detected.

items.label: AML.T0070
items.title: RAG Poisoning
items.rationale: Agent writes to vector/RAG stores through MCP tools are scanned for hidden or injected instructions before they are stored. Documents ingested outside the agent are not seen.

items.label: AML.T0072
items.title: Cyber Communication Channel
items.rationale: Reverse shells over /dev/tcp, netcat, Python, Ruby, zsh and .NET sockets and C2-style paste-site or raw-IP URLs are detected.

items.label: AML.T0074
items.title: Masquerading
items.rationale: Shadowing security-relevant commands with aliases, functions or PATH prefixes is flagged.

items.label: AML.T0075
items.title: Enterprise Resource Discovery
items.rationale: Account, group, peripheral, software and network-service enumeration commands are held for approval.

items.label: AML.T0079
items.title: Stage Capabilities
items.rationale: Fetching payloads from known staging locations (raw GitHub malware paths, paste sites, executable URLs) is flagged.

items.label: AML.T0080
items.title: AI Agent Context Poisoning
items.rationale: Requests to persist instructions in agent memory are detected; see OWASP ASI06.

items.label: AML.T0080.000
items.title: Memory
items.rationale: Memory-persistence instructions in content and in skill files are detected.

items.label: AML.T0081
items.title: Modify AI Agent Configuration
items.rationale: Edits that remove agent hooks, disable AIDR, rewrite hook/MCP/permission configuration or disable permission prompts are held or denied, and AIDR's own state is protected.

items.label: AML.T0086
items.title: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation
items.rationale: Tool inputs that send data to webhooks or external collection services are held for approval.

items.label: AML.T0089
items.title: Enterprise Environment Discovery
items.rationale: Password-policy, domain-trust, security-software and host-configuration discovery commands are held for approval.

items.label: AML.T0090
items.title: OS Credential Dumping
items.rationale: LSASS, SAM, NTDS, LSA secrets, cached credentials, DCSync, /etc/shadow and Mimikatz dumping are denied.

items.label: AML.T0094
items.title: Delay Execution of LLM Instructions
items.rationale: Content that defers instructions until a later user request ("when the user asks ... ignore") is detected.

items.label: AML.T0101
items.title: Data Destruction via AI Agent Tool Invocation
items.rationale: Recursive deletion of the root, home or system directories, disk formatting and wiping, backup and shadow-copy deletion and deletion of .env, database and .git data are denied or held.

items.label: AML.T0110.000
items.title: Definition and Instructions
items.rationale: Instruction-hijack and hidden-instruction text in skill instruction files is flagged before use.

items.label: AML.T0110.001
items.title: Implementation
items.rationale: Skill code with remote payloads, encoded execution, reverse shells, credential exfiltration, persistence or privilege escalation is flagged.

items.label: AML.T0113
items.title: Steal Web Session Cookie
items.rationale: Access to Safari and Windows browser cookie/credential stores is detected.

items.label: AML.T0123
items.title: Obfuscated Files or Information
items.rationale: Base64/hex/char-code/XOR payloads, caret and backtick obfuscation, encoded PowerShell, steganography tooling and unreviewable bytecode are detected.

items.label: AML.T0125
items.title: Create Account
items.rationale: Local and domain account creation commands are held for approval.

items.label: AML.T0127
items.title: Data Staged
items.rationale: Archiving of credential files, password-protected archives and bulk document archiving are held for approval.
